corrections.name: Mid-Atlantic Aviation Partnership

after.overview: Virginia Tech's FAA-designated UAS test-site team helps organizations design flight trials, evaluate aircraft and sensors, develop safety cases, and train operators. Its supplied briefing describes airworthiness review, custom UAS design/build/fly work, technology selection and repeatable testing. Projects can use mobile command, surveillance and weather resources at an appropriate site. MAAP describes Kentland, Central Virginia, Blackstone and Eastern Shore operating areas; these are separate from its Blacksburg office, and the supplied summaries are not current flight authorizations.
after.test_aircraft: UAS airworthiness and impact evaluation; detect-and-avoid, communications and counter-UAS sensor assessment. The supplied area briefing describes aircraft up to 1,320 lb under MAAP approvals, not unrestricted operation by other users.
after.test_dimensions: Mobile operations and engineering support with four described Virginia flight areas. Kentland has a 300-ft runway, Central Virginia uses Crewe support infrastructure, and Eastern Shore operations use Accomack County Airport. Individual flight-area records separate these resources and limitations.
after.test_access: Contact MAAP to agree on a project, site and aircraft envelope. Flight cards, risk assessment, safety review and an operations release precede testing. FAA/FCC approvals, ATC/NOTAM coordination, observers and chase-aircraft provisions depend on the specific mission and current approval.

corrections.name: Kentland Experimental Aerial Systems Laboratory

after.overview: Virginia Tech's Kentland laboratory supports fixed-wing and rotary-wing UAS research, instruction and prototype evaluation. Published infrastructure includes a 300-by-70-ft paved runway and approximately 2,000-sq-ft hangar. Research examples include wind sensing, infrastructure inspection, flight dynamics and controls. MAAP's supplied materials separately describe a Kentland flight-area outline and an up-to-700-ft-AGL limit under its test-site approval. The lab runway, the roughly 1,800-acre research farm and a flight-approval boundary are different things; none implies unrestricted public access.
after.test_aircraft: Small fixed-wing and rotary-wing aircraft for university research and instruction. MAAP's separate Kentland-area briefing describes an approval envelope up to 1,320 lb; that does not establish compatibility with the laboratory runway or availability to all users.
after.test_dimensions: 300 by 70 ft paved runway and approximately 2,000 sq ft hangar. The 1,800-acre farm is a land-resource figure; the supplied Kentland reference outline is shown separately in the MAAP flight-area layer.
after.test_access: Coordinate a research project with Virginia Tech/MAAP and confirm aircraft, launch/recovery arrangements and current approvals. The supplied reference outline does not establish public range booking or blanket flight permission.

corrections.name: Virginia Tech Counter UAS Research and Testing Center

after.overview: Virginia Tech's Counter-UAS Testing and Research Center combines instrumented outdoor trials at Kentland with laboratory and engineering work. MAAP's supplied briefing describes a 14-by-50-ft test management building, a 20-by-25-ft equipment platform elevated 20 ft with power and internet, storage and mobile-system hookups. A diverse drone library supports repeatable radar, RF, electro-optical/infrared and acoustic detection trials. Teams compare sensor tracks against aircraft truth data to study detection probability, range, accuracy, latency, alerting, data quality and human factors under terrain and day/night scenarios. Site access, aircraft eligibility and any counter-UAS mitigation authority are project-specific.
after.test_aircraft: Counter-UAS sensor characterization using commercial and custom aircraft, fixed-wing, rotary-wing and hybrid configurations. The briefing describes test targets across Groups 1-3; actual aircraft, payloads and legal authority are agreed for each project.
after.test_dimensions: 1,800-acre Kentland research farm; 14-by-50-ft (700 sq ft) test management building; 20-by-25-ft equipment platform elevated 20 ft; secure storage and large/mobile-system parking and hookups. A slide's 2,300-m scenario circle is not an authorized flight boundary or guaranteed sensor range.
after.test_access: Contact VTNSI/MAAP for government or industry testing. Agree on performance metrics, test cards, telemetry and sensor logging, safety review, approvals and release before operations. Counter-UAS research does not confer jamming or drone-defeat authority.
after.location_notes: Representative point inside the MAAP-supplied Kentland outline. The briefing places CTRC at Kentland; this is a farm-level reference, not a surveyed tower/building location, entrance or permitted launch point. Replaces the unrelated main-campus administrative pin.

corrections.name: Virginia Tech VTTI Smart Airspace Vertiport

after.overview: Virginia Tech Vertiport, FAA identifier 8VA2, is a private-use VTTI Smart Airspace node near Blacksburg. The FAA feature service records an operational heliport and provides its reference coordinates. The September 2026 briefing reports completed site improvements, Virginia private/PPR licensing and flight validation, with an instrument-procedure package submitted to the FAA. It reports Aerosonde and Electra EL2 demonstrations linking the node with Blackstone and Roanoke. A submitted procedure package is not proof of current published procedures; private-use status requires prior permission.

after.test_access: Private, prior permission required (PPR). Arrange research or demonstration operations with VTTI/MAAP and confirm current flight procedures, aircraft eligibility and approvals.
after.current_activity: September 2026 briefing reports completed site improvements, state licensing and flight validation, instrument-procedure submission, and Aerosonde/EL2 demonstrations. These are reported project milestones, not a public commercial service.

corrections.name: Virginia AAM Smart Airspace Program

after.overview: Virginia's Smart Airspace program develops infrastructure and procedures for integrating AAM aircraft into the existing IFR system. Its first described network connects Virginia Tech Vertiport (8VA2, private/PPR), Blackstone Army Airfield (KBKT, Class D/dual use) and a temporary Roanoke demonstration vertiport (KROA, Class C). The September 2026 briefing reports Aerosonde flights on the Virginia Tech-Blackstone segment in July and Electra EL2 network flights in September. It distinguishes active Blackstone procedures from submitted packages at the other nodes. The program spans several sites and is not pinned at its Richmond agency office. Proprietary approach designs and route waypoints are not published in this inventory.
after.current_activity: September 2026 briefing reports three Smart Airspace nodes, completed flight validation and Aerosonde/EL2 demonstration flights. A permanent Roanoke vertiport location and routine public service are not established by this source.
